recommended_pick.name: The 14-Day Clock, downscoped to email only, one classifier, with a measurement gate in front of it
recommended_pick.why_it_survives: It survives because after the downscope it is small enough to be honest about. It survives the do-you-even-need-AI question NARROWLY, on ONE node. A keyword filter on the shared Gmail catches the guest who writes 'I need to cancel' and misses the guest who writes 'family emergency, we won't make Saturday' or 'we're going to have to bail on the 14th', and recall is the whole point of a job defined as no money-governed message sits unseen. Reading one short, free-text, human-written message and judging whether it concerns cancelling or not showing up is unbounded phrasing on a low-occurrence pattern, which is Google PAIR's good-fit case and the one thing here a rule genuinely can't do. Everything around it is plumbing. It survives the vendor question, but only just, and only in this shape, so the deal must be month to month, cancellable, built with no FareHarbor write access, and paired in writing with the recommendation that they request the FareHarbor Agent pilot now regardless, plus a commitment that we stop billing if the vendor covers it. It survives data readiness only because the FIRST PHASE IS THE DATA WORK, with an explicit exit where we tell them the volume is too small and they build nothing further, and we would take that exit. It survives the compounding math because there is exactly ONE probabilistic step, roughly 88 to 93 percent of money-governed messages alerted at an assumed and as-yet unmeasured 90 to 95 percent classifier recall, against about 53 percent for the six-model-step version as originally pitched. It survives the cost-of-error asymmetry because it is strictly additive, it never hides, files or marks anything read, so a miss leaves them exactly where they are today, and the guest-facing message is a fixed canned line not gated on the classifier. Last, it holds the drift line. The evidence under it is one contiguous verbatim sentence the company published about its own MESSAGE CHANNEL, not a claim that anyone is overwhelmed, and the study must say channel, never strain.

downscopes_applied: Voicemail CUT from v1. The transcript source is unevidenced, nothing establishes transcription exists on 907-235-7620.

The 14-day and 24-hour STAMPING cut from v1, or it takes a FareHarbor read dependency. Days-to-departure can't be derived from an email alone, the booking date lives in FareHarbor. v1 surfaces 'possible cancellation, from this guest, referencing this date if stated' and a human does the lookup. The most impressive-sounding part of the original pick is the part its own stated architecture couldn't perform.

The guest acknowledgement UNGATED from the classifier and shipped in week one as a plain Gmail autoresponder to every inbound message in the FAQ's own wording, before any model exists. This removes a defect where every internal false positive became a customer-visible wrong message, and it doubles as the control that shows whether the model adds anything.
The classified class NARROWED to what the FAQ actually governs, cancellation and no-show risk. Date changes and party-size changes removed, no published threshold makes those money-governed.
The whole thing GATED on a two-week measurement phase whose exit criterion is a real count, with a written commitment that if the volume is small we say so and they build nothing.
The RICE reach claim of '100 percent of money-governed messages are routed' STRUCK. That is a perfect-recall claim made before a single message has been labeled.

verdicts_summary.The 14-Day Clock: downscope, and it is the survivor
verdicts_summary.Front-desk voice agent on the one line: KILL, on four independent grounds. The honest need clears at the rules tier with a published text number, voicemail-to-email or a human answering service, all phone-company purchases rather than builds. It duplicates FareHarbor Agent's stated function on a platform they already pay for. Its only supporting outcome evidence is a vendor-published car-rental case study. The compounding math gives single-digit to low-tens end-to-end success on a full call, and the MDPI study points the same way on the exact channel where weather and refunds land.
verdicts_summary.Standby seat filler: downscope, and rename it honestly. It is a database query, a templated SMS and a first-come lock, with NO AI in it at all. It must not be sold as an AI build or carry an AI price. Later lane, behind express written consent capture and a list with enough names to be worth firing.
verdicts_summary.Off-season desk and 2027 book: downscope. Kill the RAG chatbot, keep the job. 'Digital employee' is agent-washing for a retrieval chatbot and the label must not reach the study. What clears at the rules tier is an off-season autoresponder pointing at the FAQ, a next-season interest form, and one scheduled send when 2027 dates open. Days of work, no model.
verdicts_summary.Weather-day fan-out console: downscope. Keep the shape, remove the AI. Per-party templates plus a merge with a human on the send button, because a template can't invent a refund figure and a model can. The MDPI study endorses this exact human-gated design. Sequence after the Clock, it inherits a FareHarbor dependency.
verdicts_summary.Do nothing and pilot FareHarbor Agent: KEEP as a parallel recommendation in the study, and say out loud that we recommend they ask FareHarbor for the pilot now whether or not they hire us. Its RICE 40 must not be presented against the Clock's 85 as a comparison, it scores that way only because effort is near zero and the two are not commensurable.

where_not_to_use_ai: Most of this build is not an AI problem and we will not price it as one. The date math against the 14-day and 24-hour lines is arithmetic and belongs in code, never in a model, so a deadline can't be hallucinated and every case can be unit tested. The guest acknowledgement is one canned sentence in the wording already on their own FAQ, sent by a plain Gmail autoresponder to every inbound message, which means it can't be a wrong answer, it needs no classifier, and it ships in week one before any model exists. Which refund rule applies on a weather day, 100 percent before departure against $30 per person after leaving the dock, is a two-branch conditional straight out of their published policy, and the per-party weather notification is a mail merge with a human on the send button, because a template can't invent a refund figure and a model can. Filling a freed seat, once a consented list exists, is a database query, a templated text and a lock. Being reachable while a captain is on the water is a published text number, voicemail-to-email or a human answering service, which are phone-company purchases rather than software. Answering the same twenty pre-trip questions is what their FAQ already does, and it is the one place FareHarbor Agent is explicitly described as operating on a platform they already pay for, so we will not sell it to them under any name. Five of the six candidates on the table clear their own bar at the rules tier with no model in them at all. The single node where a language model genuinely earns its place is reading one short, messy, human-written message and judging whether it is about cancelling or not showing up, because people write that a hundred different ways and no keyword list catches them all. One model call, on one node, with an eval set behind it and a human on every consequence.
step_math_headline: One probabilistic step by design. Roughly 88 to 93 percent of money-governed messages alerted at an ASSUMED 90 to 95 percent classifier recall, which is an assumption until an eval set exists. The six-model-step version as originally pitched computes to about 53 percent end to end and is unshippable. Cutting the model to one node is what makes the number survivable.
honest_flags: Unevidenced capability in the original pick, 'voicemail transcripts they already have'. Nothing establishes transcription exists. Cut from v1, confirming what the carrier provides is a task and not an assumption.

Internal contradiction in the original v1, it promised to stamp against the 14-day and 24-hour lines while also promising read-only on a mailbox with no FareHarbor access. Days-to-departure can't be derived from an email alone.

There is NO BASELINE for anything, anywhere. No messages per day, no cancellations per season, no calls, no after-hours volume, no weather days, no off-season inquiries, no attach rate, NO CHARTER PRICE. Every impact figure is an index rather than a measurement. No ROI may be stated except as conditional on a count that does not yet exist, and the STUDY MUST SAY THAT IN THE ROI SECTION rather than only in a footnote.
No labeled data and no eval set exist, so the classifier has no acceptance metric today. Any accuracy figure must be labeled an assumption to be replaced by a measured number at the end of phase one.

Design defect found and corrected, the guest auto-acknowledgement was gated on the classifier, turning every internal false positive into a customer-visible wrong message telling a guest to phone in a cancellation they never made.

False-trust failure mode. A system that pings for the urgent ones can quietly stop people scanning the inbox, at which point a miss is worse than no system. Strictly additive, never marks read, never files, never hides, and the digest lists everything that arrived rather than the leftovers.

Alert routing defect. Ringing both owners assumes both can act. One is published as Owner and Captain of The Irish and is structurally at sea with paying guests, where an alert is an interruption he can't act on. Route to the office manager first, escalate to the captain only on no-acknowledgement, cap alerts per day.
Scope inflation against the published policy. Date changes and party-size changes have no published threshold and were removed.

PII gate, not a footnote. Guest messages carry names, phone numbers, party details and possibly payment references. A written data-processing agreement, provider retention disabled, and the owners' explicit informed consent are week-one scope. A family business mailing us a password is not a plan.

Vendor risk is the largest commercial risk in the package and is NOT fully retired by the downscope. Operator alerting is an easier feature for FareHarbor to add than the guest-facing agent they already shipped, and FareHarbor Agent is described as covering email.
Sampling limitation. Three to four weeks of late August is peak season. A classifier and a baseline built on that window are validated for August only.
Consent exposure on the standby filler. Texting people who once inquired is not covered by documented consent and the penalty regime is per message.
Agent-washing in the candidate list. 'Digital employee' described a retrieval chatbot. The label must not reach the study.
Score comparability. Do-nothing scores RICE 40 only because its effort is near zero. Presenting 85 against 40 as a verdict would be misleading.

THE HONEST CEILING IS SMALL. If phase one counts a handful of cancellations a season, the correct output of this Field Study is that they should buy nothing from us, keep the free autoresponder, and ask FareHarbor for the pilot. That outcome must be WRITTEN INTO THE PROPOSAL as a real exit rather than implied, because a measurement gate nobody would actually honour is worse than no gate.
